title: Simplicial reversal preserves Joyal homotopy data and horn-lifting classes
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, horns, quasicategories and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], categorical equivalences and Joyal fibrations of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and Kan fibrations of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ put $\alpha^\vee(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$. Define $K^{\mathrm{op}}_n=K_n$ with operator $K^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)=K(\alpha^\vee)$, and $f^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the same degreewise components as $f$. This is a covariant involution. Opposite preserves and reflects Kan complexes, Kan fibrations, quasicategories and inner fibrations, and interchanges horn $i$ with horn $n-i$ under the standard simplex-reversal identification. For arbitrary small simplicial sets $A,C$ there is a natural simplicial isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},C^{\mathrm{op}})\cong\operatorname{Fun}(A,C)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
compatible with composition and with $h(K^{\mathrm{op}})\cong(hK)^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $h$ is the vertex-edge category in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Opposite preserves and reflects categorical equivalences and Joyal fibrations, including maps whose domain or codomain is not a quasicategory. It preserves degreewise pullbacks and takes fibrant cospans with Joyal fibration legs to cospans of the same kind.
